choices.label: Cancel the Lavi and buy more F-16s (Peres plan)
choices.note: Foreign Minister Shimon Peres's plan, adopted by the unity cabinet 12-11; Finance Minister Moshe Nissim broke with Likud to back halting the project.

cite.claim: Cabinet adopted Peres's plan to scrap the Lavi 12-11
cite.quote: By a vote of 12 to 11 the Cabinet adopted a plan by Foreign Minister Shimon Peres to scrap the seven-year-old Lavi program

cite.claim: Finance Minister Nissim backed halting the Lavi
cite.quote: Finance Minister Moshe Nissim, of the Likud bloc, broke ranks with his party and insisted on halting the Lavi

choices.label: Continue building the Lavi
choices.note: Position of most Likud ministers led by Prime Minister Shamir; Moshe Arens, the plane's staunchest cabinet advocate, announced he would resign after losing the vote.

cite.claim: Most Likud ministers led by Shamir voted to continue the Lavi

cite.claim: Arens was the staunchest advocate of the Lavi

patches.why: Choices audit: every option now carries source+cite naming who decided/advocated it (Peres/Nissim vs Shamir/Arens).

choices.label: Hold fire at US request and accept Patriot batteries
choices.note: Prime Minister Shamir's decision: Israel reserved the right to retaliate but did not strike back, while the US rushed Patriot batteries to Israel.

cite.claim: Shamir-led cabinet did not strike back
cite.quote: Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir leads the Cabinet in an all-day emergency session, but, despite reserving the right to retaliate, Israel does not strike back.

cite.claim: US sent Patriot batteries
cite.quote: the United States rushes Patriot anti-missile batteries to Israel

cite.claim: Baker credits Shamir with the restraint
cite.quote: it wouldn't have happened frankly had it not been for Yitzak Shamir, the Prime Minister who was under great pressure to respond and retaliate

choices.label: Launch a retaliatory air operation against Iraq
choices.note: Defence Minister Moshe Arens pressed for retaliation; US Secretary of State James Baker later recalled that Arens felt Shamir had made the wrong decision.

cite.claim: Arens felt Shamir was wrong not to retaliate
cite.quote: Well Arens was just really of the view that I think he felt that his Prime Minister had made the wrong decision in not retaliating.

patches.why: Choices audit: added option-level sources (CIE timeline, PBS Frontline Baker interview naming Shamir and Arens).

choices.label: Recognise the PLO and sign the Declaration of Principles

cite.quote: the Knesset approved by a vote of 61-50 the accord signed last week in Washington by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization.

cite.claim: Rabin welcomed the margin and moved to implement
cite.quote: Rabin said after the vote that he was satisfied with the margin of victory and that it gave the government the confidence it needs to begin implementing the agreement.

choices.label: Reject the accord with the PLO
choices.note: The position of the Likud opposition: its leader Benjamin Netanyahu called on the party to stand firm against the accord.

choices.label: Withdraw unilaterally to the international border
choices.note: Barak pledged to leave Lebanon within a year; the cabinet endorsed withdrawal by 7 July 2000, and the pull-out was completed on 24 May after the SLA collapsed.

cite.claim: Cabinet endorsed Barak's plan to withdraw by 7 July 2000
cite.quote: On March 5, 2000, the Israeli cabinet unanimously endorsed Barak’s plan to withdraw by July 7, 2000.

cite.claim: Barak vowed to withdraw by July regardless of a Syria deal
cite.quote: he vowed to withdraw Israeli troops from southern Lebanon by July

choices.label: Stay in the security zone until a security arrangement (e.g. with Syria) is reached
choices.note: The earlier policy: in 1998 Prime Minister Netanyahu rejected calls for a unilateral pull-out, saying troops would stay until an arrangement guaranteed the northern border's security.

cite.claim: Netanyahu: troops stay until an arrangement guarantees security
cite.quote: saying Israeli soldiers would remain in south Lebanon until an arrangement could be found which would guarantee the security of Israel’s northern border.

cite.claim: A withdrawal after a Syria agreement was seen as preferable
cite.quote: From the Israeli standpoint, a withdrawal from Lebanon after reaching an agreement with Syria

patches.why: Choices audit: removed 'illustrative game values' text and the invented casualty range; added option-level sources (CRS, JTA, Tribune/DPA quoting Netanyahu).

choices.label: Carry out unilateral disengagement
choices.note: Prime Minister Sharon's plan; the Knesset approved it 67-45 in October 2004 with Labor and Yahad support while nearly half of Likud's faction opposed it.

cite.claim: Knesset approved Sharon's plan to withdraw from Gaza
cite.quote: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon won a resounding victory in the Knesset for his plan to withdraw from the Gaza Strip and part of the West Bank

cite.claim: Vote 67-45
cite.quote: Sharon mustered 67 votes for his disengagement plan, with 45 against and 7 abstentions.

choices.label: Put disengagement to a national referendum first
choices.note: Demanded by Finance Minister Netanyahu and Likud ministers Livnat, Katz and Naveh, and by the National Religious Party; Sharon rejected it.

cite.claim: Netanyahu and three Likud ministers sought a referendum commitment
cite.quote: working on a proposal to condition their support in Tuesday’s Knesset vote on a commitment by Sharon to hold a national referendum on disengagement.

cite.claim: NRP ultimatum: hold a referendum
cite.quote: served the prime minister with an ultimatum: Hold a referendum or else.

choices.label: Keep the Gaza settlements
choices.note: The position of the National Religious Party and the Likud rebels who opposed the plan outright.

cite.claim: NRP opposed disengagement
cite.quote: The National Religious Party, which is part of Sharon’s government but which opposes disengagement

cite.claim: Almost half of Likud's Knesset faction opposed it
cite.quote: opposed by almost half of the Knesset faction of his own Likud Party

patches.why: Choices audit: dropped the unsourced 'negotiated withdrawal with the PA' option (no named advocate found); added the documented referendum demand; all options sourced.

Choices audit: no named advocate at the time of a 'limited strikes' alternative was found. choices.label: Approve a limited 10-month moratorium (excluding East Jerusalem and ongoing projects)
choices.note: Netanyahu's offer, approved by the security cabinet on 25 November 2009; US envoy Mitchell said it fell short of a full freeze.

cite.quote: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu offered the Palestinians a 10-month moratorium on building new Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank Wednesday

cite.claim: Approved by the security cabinet
cite.quote: It was approved by Israel's security cabinet today.

choices.label: Reject any freeze and continue building
choices.note: Position of West Bank settler leaders, who told Netanyahu they would keep opposing the freeze and resist stop-work orders.

cite.claim: Settler leaders vowed to oppose the freeze
cite.quote: West Bank settler leaders told Israel’s prime minister that they would continue to oppose the building freeze and resist stop-work orders.

choices.label: Accept a full freeze including East Jerusalem
choices.note: The Palestinian demand: the PA refused to enter negotiations until a full freeze was in place; Israel refused limits in East Jerusalem.

cite.claim: Palestinians refused talks until a full freeze
cite.quote: Netanyahu's refusal to implement a full settlement freeze and the Palestinians refusal to enter negotiations until such a freeze is in place.

cite.claim: Mitchell: offer falls short of a full freeze
cite.quote: It falls short of a full settlement freeze, but it is more than any Israeli government has done before

patches.why: Choices audit: added option-level sources (ABC News; JTA on settler leaders).

choices.note: Netanyahu announced the committee on 7 August 2011; the cabinet later approved its report 21-8.

cite.quote: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu established a committee to examine the demands of leaders of the social justice protest movement

choices.label: Negotiate directly with the protest leaders
choices.note: What protest leaders asked for instead of a committee: direct dialogue with the prime minister.

cite.quote: Protest leaders have already decried the committee, saying that they are looking for direct dialogue with Netanyahu.

patches.why: Choices audit: dropped the unsourced 'hold the line on the budget' option (no named advocate found) and replaced it with the protest leaders' documented demand; all options sourced.

choices.label: Accept the Egyptian-mediated deal: 1,027 prisoners for Shalit
choices.note: Approved by the cabinet 26-3 in an emergency session on 11 October 2011.

patches.why: Choices audit: added option-level sources naming the ministers on each side.

choices.label: After Hamas rejects the Egyptian ceasefire, expand into a ground operation against tunnels
choices.note: Israel's security cabinet accepted Egypt's ceasefire proposal on 15 July 2014 and Hamas reportedly rejected it; on 17 July Netanyahu and Defence Minister Ya'alon ordered a ground operation against cross-border tunnels.

cite.quote: Rockets fired from Gaza continued to land in populated areas of Israel after its security Cabinet accepted and put into effect an Egyptian proposal for a cease-fire.

cite.claim: Hamas reportedly rejected it
cite.quote: Hamas reportedly rejected the cease-fire proposal, calling it unacceptable.

cite.claim: Netanyahu and Ya'alon ordered the ground operation against tunnels
cite.quote: following the order given by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Moshe Yaalon.

choices.label: Keep to air and naval strikes and press the Egyptian ceasefire track without a ground phase
choices.note: The Obama administration said it would oppose a ground incursion. A ceasefire was not Israel's choice alone: Israel had accepted Egypt's 15 July proposal, which Hamas rejected.

cite.claim: Obama administration would oppose a ground incursion
cite.quote: The Obama administration, which during the conflict has backed Israel’s right to defend itself, has said it would oppose a ground incursion.

patches.why: Critic framing fix: Israel accepted Egypt's 15 July ceasefire and Hamas rejected it, which is now stated in the historical option; the alternative no longer implies an early ceasefire was Israel's choice alone; all options sourced.

cite.quote: reported that the strikes were “limited” in scope and did not target Iran’s nuclear facilities.

cite.claim: Netanyahu insisted Israel decides its response
cite.quote: Netanyahu insisted that Israel, not its allies, would determine its response to the missile attack.

cite.quote: Israel had indicated that it would retaliate directly against Iran despite warnings from the Biden administration not to do so.

choices.label: Strike military targets: air defences and missile production
choices.note: Israel's target set on 26 October 2024; Biden had urged a response that limited escalation.

cite.claim: Targets were missile/drone production and air defences
cite.quote: The military said later it had completed its “targeted” attacks in Iran, striking missile and drone manufacturing facilities and launch sites as well as surface-to-air missile arrays.

cite.claim: No energy or nuclear targets
cite.quote: Targets did not include energy infrastructure or Iran’s nuclear facilities.

choices.label: Strike Iran's nuclear programme and energy facilities
choices.note: Urged publicly by former prime minister Naftali Bennett on 1 October 2024; the Biden administration warned Israel against hitting oil fields or nuclear sites.

cite.claim: Bennett urged destroying Iran's nuclear programme and energy facilities
cite.quote: “We must act *now* to destroy Iran’s nuclear program, its central energy facilities, and to fatally cripple this terrorist regime.”

cite.claim: Biden warned against oil and nuclear targets
cite.quote: Biden was warning Israel not to target installations that could escalate into all-out war, including Iran’s oil fields, its nuclear reactors

patches.why: Choices audit: added option-level sources naming Bennett (advocate) and the US position.

choices.label: Accept the US-French ceasefire

cite.claim: Security cabinet approved 10-1
cite.quote: The national security cabinet officially approves a ceasefire by a majority of 10 ministers to one, says the Prime Minister’s Office.

cite.claim: Mutual self-defence clause
cite.quote: these commitments do not preclude either Israel or Lebanon from exercising their inherent right of self-defence, consistent with international law

cite.claim: Netanyahu's reading
cite.quote: Prime Minister Netanyahu said on Tuesday night that Israel would “maintain full freedom of military action” in Lebanon

cite.claim: Lebanon's objection
cite.quote: But Lebanese officials said they would oppose any violations of Lebanon’s sovereignty.

choices.label: Reject the ceasefire and keep fighting Hezbollah
choices.note: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir was the only security cabinet member to vote against the deal.

cite.claim: Ben Gvir sole vote against
cite.quote: The sole security cabinet member to vote against the deal was National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

patches.why: Critic framing fix: 'freedom to act' is no longer presented as a term of the deal; the note quotes the mutual self-defence clause, attributes the broad reading to Netanyahu and records Lebanon's objection; the alternative is attributed to Ben Gvir's vote against.
